data.why: Whatnot opened its new European headquarters in Dublin just three weeks ago, marking a major international expansion. For a CFO, entering new geographies triggers a surge in local suppliers, regional tax requirements, and vendor approval routing.
data.angle: Managing new international supplier onboarding and AP approvals across European operations.

not_chosen.reason: Bad news: headline alleges Whatnot operates like a casino and faces an investigation by the American justice system.
Bad news: reports Whatnot ending seller coverage for USPS shipping adjustments, which reflects cost cuts and negative seller sentiment.
Series G funding took place in August 2026, which is older than 90 days.
Kristin has been in the CFO seat for over five months, so commenting on her appointment is old and tells her her own life.
Annual employee headcount growth of 35% is a broad metric rather than a specific timely event.

data.subject: dublin hq
data.body:
Hi Kristin,

Saw Whatnot opened a new European HQ in Dublin.

Setting up operations across Europe usually brings a wave of new local suppliers and bills to sort through. Who is matching and approving all those invoices today?

Instacart cut AP approval time from 2 weeks to 2 days with Zamp.

Open to seeing how?

[Your name]
